differences.justification: Deprecated for removal since 1.9.0, when it moved to the langchain4j-guardrails module; the replacement is dev.langchain4j.guardrails.JsonExtractorOutputGuardrail. Removing it also takes two public constructors taking Jackson's ObjectMapper and TypeReference out of core's API, which a caller cannot satisfy under Jackson 3.

differences.new: method java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture dev.langchain4j.guardrail.GuardrailExecutor, R extends dev.langchain4j.guardrail.GuardrailResult, G extends dev.langchain4j.guardrail.Guardrail, E extends dev.langchain4j.observability.api.event.GuardrailExecutedEvent>::executeAsync(P)
differences.justification: GuardrailExecutor is a sealed interface that only permits AbstractGuardrailExecutor (implemented within langchain4j-core), so no external code can implement it. Adding the non-blocking executeAsync counterpart is therefore not a breaking change for API consumers; revapi does not model interface sealing.

UnsupportedFeatureException now extends NonRetriableException instead of extending LangChain4jException directly. NonRetriableException is itself a LangChain4jException, so the type is still assignable everywhere it was before and every existing catch clause keeps compiling and catching; only an intermediate supertype is inserted. The behavioural effect is that RetryUtils stops retrying it, which is the intended fix: a provider that does not support a feature will not begin to support it on a retry, so the retries only added latency before the same failure.

This constructor is a new overload that accepts the optional EmbeddingInputMapper. It was added next to the existing public constructor, not widened from a previously private member; revapi reports the visibility increase because a private constructor with the same arity existed before. The class is not designed for subclassing, and the previous constructor remains unchanged, so no existing caller is affected.
